data.name: Ghanasyaam
data.gender_notes: Ghanasyaam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ghanasyaam is a Sanskrit name derived from the root 'Ghan' meaning 'protector'. This name is bestowed upon a child born to a protective father or to one who embodies the qualities of protection and strength. The name Ghanasyaam carries the meaning “He who protects” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ghanasyaam usually hope their child will grow to embody he who protects and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ghanasyaam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “He who protects.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghanasyaam total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Ghanasyaam was a renowned Hindu scholar and philosopher of the 12th century AD. He was born in the southern Indian state of Karnataka and studied under the great philosopher Shankara. Ghanasyaam is best known for his contributions to the field of Advaita Vedanta, particularly his commentary on the Vedanta Sutras known as the Bhashya or Tattvabodhini commentary.

historical_references.reference: Ghanasyaam was also a significant figure in the development of Sanskrit literature in the 13th century AD.
